slides.title: Integrating Channels Around the HCP
bullets: Defines how in-person, virtual, digital, and network channels integrate
Centered on the HCP's experience, not managed as isolated channel efforts
Introduced here at the strategy level; developed fully in a later module

slides.title: HCPs Already Move Fluidly Across Channels
bullets: HCPs combine an MSL conversation, a recommended publication, and a webinar
They also follow content on professional networks, often in the same week
They expect a consistent experience, with no contradictions across channels

slides.title: Channels Complement, Digital Doesn't Replace the MSL
bullets: Digital content can spark initial interest deepened later in a personal visit
A personal visit can surface a need later resolved with personalized content
Digital channels sustain contact with HCPs who get fewer in-person visits

slides.title: One Calendar, One Message, One View of Each Stakeholder
bullets: Field activity, digital communication, and education platforms share a plan
They share the same calendar and the same evidence-based scientific message
This avoids fragmented, uncoordinated contact toward the same KOL

slides.title: Fitting Field Work into a Bigger Journey
bullets: Doesn't require taking on digital channel management responsibilities
Requires understanding how your field activity fits the HCP's wider journey
Includes recommending relevant digital content when it's the better fit

takeaway.title: The omnichannel medical plan makes every HCP channel work as one coherent experience
bullets: It exists because HCPs already move fluidly between channels themselves
Digital content and personal visits are designed to complement, not replace
Coordination across channels prevents fragmented, uncoordinated stakeholder contact
